Issued at 103 PM CDT Tue Oct 6 2026

Today - Friday: Mostly Dry, Near to Slightly Above Normal Temps

Northwest flow continues across the region through the end of 
the week with little synoptic forcing expected to traverse the 
mean flow resulting in an overall dry forecast for the area. 
That said, there are two periods of interest from a precipitation
perspective: Wednesday night into Thursday morning and Friday. 

During the first period, model guidance depicts increasing 700-
500hPa differential positive vorticity advection sneaking into 
northern Wisconsin which could spark some scattered showers. The
main point of uncertainty is a lack of saturation given dry air
below 6-7kft due to fairly deep mixing expected Wednesday 
afternoon. CAM guidance also keeps the bulk of any precipitation
north of our area while the 06.12z HREF/REFS suggest a 10-30% 
chance for those north of I-94. As of right now, have tended 
towards a dry forecast given the issues with the dry air. 

The second period is also a bit uncertain. Southerly flow 
developing across the central Great Plains on Friday gives way 
to an 850hPa low level jet and associated warm air advection/moisture
transport that have the potential to nose into the Upper 
Mississippi River Valley. However, ensemble guidance is a bit 
varied on the location of precipitation associated with this 
feature, if it develops at all. The European model suite is the
most excited regarding precipitation probabilities (30-50%) 
given a further northward placement of the low level jet 
whereas the the GEFS/AIGEFS/GEPS solutions tend a little drier 
across our area (10-20%) and keep precipitation largely to our 
south. Have stuck with the 06.13z NBM solution which is more in
line with the GEFS/AIGEFS/GEPS at 10-20%, but if a clear 
northward trend is noted then probabilities will likely 
increase. 

Outside of the low potential for precipitation through the rest
of the week, a weak surface front moving through the region 
today/tonight will shift our winds to the northwest and usher in
some slightly cooler temperatures for Wednesday and Thursday. 
Depending on how far northward the low level jet is able to make
it, a warming trend may be able to start as early as Friday 
which is currently the favored solution of the 06.13z NBM.

This Weekend - Early Next Week: Brief Warm Up, Precipitation 
Potential Returns

The upper level synoptic pattern begins to break down this 
weekend as ridging across the western United States begins to 
shift eastward while model guidance depicts a longwave trough 
moving onshore the West Coast. Rising heights associated with 
the approaching ridge and the aforementioned southerly flow 
associated with cyclogenesis occurring as the trough moves 
onshore should lead to a bit of a warm up by this weekend with 
the 06.13z NBM mean suggesting temperatures climb into the mid 
to upper 70s areawide Saturday, 15-20 degrees above normal for 
this time of year, while some locations possibly reach 80 
degrees (40-60%). Fairly little spread exists in the 25th-75th 
percentiles of the NBM membership, backed up by other ensemble 
suites such as the GEFS/EPS/GEPS and their AI equivalents, so 
confidence in these warmer temperatures is high. 

Heading into early next week, the potential for precipitation 
returns to the Upper Midwest, but confidence in the overall 
forecast is not very high at this point as quite a bit of 
variability exists amongst the previously mentioned ensemble 
suites regarding timing and location of precipitation. That 
said, a fair number of members do suggest there is some 
potential for precipitation to start off the new week, so have 
continued with the 06.13z NBM mean which is around 20-50%. 
Cooler temperatures also look to make a return, falling back 
towards normal by Tuesday.
